historical_references.context: Ibn Battuta was a renowned traveler from Morocco who explored Asia and Africa in the 14th century. He made a note of a city called Aana in his travelogue.

historical_references.reference: Aana was also known as 'Ana or 'Amna in medieval Arabic texts, and was an important trading center between Egypt and Nubia.
historical_references.context: Aana was a significant city in the Nile Valley, located between the regions of Egypt and Nubia. It served as a major trading center and played an essential role in the exchange of goods between these two civilizations.
